offence_severity: Death (Section 302) - Minimum 10 years, Maximum Life Imprisonment or Death; Section 201 - Minimum 6 months, Maximum 2 years
number_of_offences: Two offences charged (Section 302 and 201), both upheld by the High Court but overturned on appeal
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the circumstantial evidence, including the recovery of the dead body of the deceased based on the alleged confessional statement of the appellant, but found it insufficient to establish guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the witnesses, noting that there was no specific identification mark on the recovered sheep to link them to the deceased, and that the recovery of the dead body was based on a confessional statement which was denied by the appellant.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 27.01.2000; Trial judgment: 3rd July, 2015; High Court decision: 27.02.2006; Supreme Court decision: 11.10.2018
legal_representation: Annam D. N. Rao, A. Venkatesh, Rahul Mishra, Advs. for the Appellant; S. Udaya Kumar Sagar, Mrityunjai Singh, Mrs. D. Bharathi Reddy, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: Case registered under Section 379 of the Indian Penal Code; charge sheet filed under Sections 302/201 I.P.C.
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and sentence affirmed; High Court: Conviction and sentence affirmed; Supreme Court: Conviction set aside, appellant acquitted
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant sold three sheep to Lingaiah (PW-5), who in turn sold them to Shaik Naseem (PW-9), and that the dead body of the deceased-Ramesh was recovered from under a culvert based on the appellant's alleged confessional statement.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the appellant denied making a confessional statement and that the recovery of the dead body was at his behest. They also pointed out that the sheep recovered did not have distinct identification marks to link them to the deceased-Ramesh, and that the motive for murder (theft of sheep) was not proven.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that when a case rests on circumstantial evidence, such evidence must satisfy three tests: (i) the circumstances must be cogently and firmly established; (ii) they must tend unerringly towards the guilt of the accused; and (iii) they must form a complete chain pointing to the accused as the only possible perpetrator.
precedent_relied_upon: S.D. Soni v. State of Gujarat (1992) Supp 1 SCC 567; Venkatesan v. State of Tamil Nadu (2008) 8 SCC 456; Raj Kumar Singh alias Raju Alias Batya v. State of Rajasthan (2013) 5 SCC 722
other_sentence_order: The appellant is acquitted of all the charges and is ordered to be released forthwith unless his presence is required in any other case.
